A_target.statement:
Let $A$ be a [[Definition:Type|type]] and $B$ a type family over $A$.
The [[Definition:Dependent Sum Type|dependent sum type]] $\displaystyle \sum_{x : A} \map B x$ has pairs $\tuple {a, b}$ with $a : A$ and $b : \map B a$, and projections:
:$\mathsf {fst}: \displaystyle \sum_{x : A} \map B x \to A$
:$\mathsf {snd}: \map {\mathsf {snd} } p : \map B {\map {\mathsf {fst} } p}$

B_source.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be [[Definition:Type|types]].
The [[Definition:Product Type|product type]] $A \times B$ has pairs $\tuple {a, b}$ and projections:
:$\mathsf {fst}: A \times B \to A$
:$\mathsf {snd}: A \times B \to B$

substitutions.the second component's fixed type: a type family indexed by the first component
substitutions.the projection to the second factor: a projection whose type depends on the first projection

derived.the two projections: the same two projections, with the second having a dependent type

object_map.reformulation: Let the type of the second component depend on the value of the first, generalizing the fixed second factor.

validity_conditions: The ordinary product is the case where the family is constant, so the generalization is faithful and the notation specializes correctly.
The second projection can only be typed after the first has been applied, since its type mentions the first component; this ordering is essential and has no counterpart in the nondependent case.
The eliminator must be stated in the dependent form to prove properties of arbitrary pairs, since the simple projections alone do not give the induction principle.
proof_plan: Replace the fixed second type $B$ by a type family $\map B x$ indexed by the first component.
Form pairs $\tuple {a, b}$ with $b : \map B a$.

Define $\map {\mathsf {fst} } {a, b} = a$ as before.
Define $\map {\mathsf {snd} } {a, b} = b$, with type $\map B {\map {\mathsf {fst} } p}$ depending on the first component.
